scope: Optional five-line biblical comparison for a B1 lexical chiasm lesson; selected-clause adaptation, not a full study or full text quotation
numbering: The Hebrew edition counts the superscription as verse 1. Reader-facing citations use English verse numbering.

claims.statement: The praise refrains at English verses 3 and 5 repeat exactly; blessing returns at verses 1, 6, and 7.
Blessing units surround repeated praise refrains, which surround the nations’ joy, just judgment, and guidance at verse 4.
claims.limits: Outer sections do not match clause for clause. The reading does not prove an exclusive theological climax.

adaptation.title: A five-part biblical comparison
adaptation.notice: Selected-clause English adaptation, not the full psalm. Verse numbers follow the English edition.
adaptation.explanation: Bless frames the example; praise returns on either side of the guiding line. The full poem supports a five-part concentric reading: verses 1–2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6–7.
adaptation.omissions: This short selection omits mercy, the shining face, salvation, parts of the refrain, joy, fair judgment, harvest, worldwide reverence, and Selah.

review: Primary text independently checked by source agent and parent; selected boundaries and omissions labelled.
